The title of this post is not really consistent with the report. It makes no claims about millions of voters and the one study with a sample of 14 is simply one of a number of studies cited. Furthermore, none of the studies is cited to support any particular level of illegal voting. They simply support that voter registration (and voting) by illegals does occur, and may very well occur in numbers that can affect the outcome of elections, especially in smaller races.

Since the report is not making the claims trying to be refuted, and since no one else is actually studying the issue in any comprehensive, competent way, I do not see any great weight to the letter from others refuting it. First, that is not how science is accomplished. They are simply playing a game of he said, she said. Second, the report does, in fact, contain adequate information to conclude there actually are illegals who register to vote and then actually do so. What it lacks is any reliable indicator of the scope of that problem. But whether it is 1%, 6% or 16%, it is still a problem.
